title: Comparable corpus scale
caption: All retained news triplets are included; no status-based partition is used.

title: Knowledge-graph breadth
caption: The corpora are similar in row scale but encode different knowledge functions.

title: Confidence distributions
caption: Confidence is preserved as supplied and is the only model-quality signal used for news rankings.

title: News confidence by food pool
caption: The three pools have similar confidence distributions; counts and food-specific evidence drive substantive differences.

title: News-triplet coverage by food pool
caption: Article counts measure corpus representation, not incident prevalence.

title: Dominant predicates reveal different corpus functions
caption: FSSAI baseline emphasizes standards and definitions; news emphasizes incidents, adulterants, effects, places and actions.

title: Normalized overlap is sparse
caption: Exact overlap is conservative; terminology and role differences can hide contextual overlap.

title: Most reported food-adulterant relationships
caption: Ranks use unique articles and retain the explicitly named affected food.

title: Most reported relationships in the Oil article pool
caption: Food is taken from the triplet; the pool only identifies the source collection.

title: Most reported relationships in the Ghee article pool
caption: Food is taken from the triplet; the pool only identifies the source collection.

title: Most reported relationships in the Milk article pool
caption: Food is taken from the triplet; the pool only identifies the source collection.

title: Food-specific adulterant article matrix
caption: The same candidate is not assumed equally likely across foods.

title: Recurrence and confidence are complementary signals
caption: Confidence ranks extraction certainty; recurrence measures corpus repetition and can include duplicate incident coverage.

title: FSSAI baseline representation classes
caption: Absence means absent from the supplied verified baseline, not necessarily from every current FSSAI document.

title: Priority candidates combine recurrence, confidence and local health links
caption: The score is a transparent discovery heuristic, not a risk or prevalence estimate.

title: Candidate-specific test representation
caption: A missing graph edge triggers method retrieval and validation; it does not prove no test exists.

title: Most represented health effects in news triplets
caption: These are reported effects in the local corpus, not incidence estimates.

title: Health-effect representation by source food pool
caption: Pool-level differences reflect corpus composition and repeated coverage.

title: Directly joined food-adulterant-effect chains
caption: Both graph edges occur in the same article and share the canonical adulterant node.

title: Causal-chain evidence levels
caption: Repository-inferred chains are hypotheses and are separated from same-article direct joins.

title: Candidate presence given Milk and renal-failure context
caption: The percentage is an article association share, not a diagnostic or causal probability.

title: Food specificity of leading adulterant candidates
caption: This directly answers whether a candidate is represented across foods or concentrated in one food matrix.

title: Publication-year coverage by food pool
caption: Publication date is not incident date; 2026 is partial and collection intensity varies.

title: Publication trajectories of leading candidates
caption: Trends describe the collected corpus and repeated reporting, not population prevalence.

title: Most represented regulatory-action relations
caption: Action relations complement food chemistry by showing what authorities or operators did.

title: Most represented news detection and method relations
caption: News-only method language; a method mention is not automatically a validated food-specific protocol.

title: News-source concentration
caption: Concentrated sourcing can amplify repeated incidents and editorial framing.

title: Sensitivity to confidence thresholds
caption: Threshold views are reported alongside the all-triplet result; no historical status field is used.

title: Leading directly joined causal-chain network
caption: Blue nodes are foods, gold nodes are adulterants, and red nodes are effects.
